0.0.n: Introduces a contrast with what was said before.

0.2.n: Refers to what the word expresses, rather than how it sounds.

0.3.n: Marks 意味 as what differs.

0.4.n: Often used with negatives, but here strengthens 違います to emphasize a total difference.

0.5.n: The polite form of 違う, ending in ます.

0.6.n: Adds emphasis, presenting the difference as information the listener should notice.

1.0.n: A country name; followed by で to locate this usage.

1.1.n: Marks Japan as the place where this word usage applies.

1.3.n: Borrowed from Viking, this word refers to an all-you-can-eat buffet in Japanese.

1.5.n: Marks バイキング as the topic being explained.

1.7.n: Combines 食べ, from 食べる, with 放題, which expresses freedom to do something without limits.

1.9.n: Introduces the explanation before ことです; the whole expression gives a definition here.

1.10.n: Packages 食べ放題 as the content of the definition in ということです.

1.11.n: Politely finishes the explanation; ということです means that this is what the term signifies.

2.1.n: The quoted expression is being defined across this line and the next two.

2.3.n: Marks 食べ放題 as the topic of the definition.

2.4.n: Specifies that payment happens one time before the eating described next.

2.5.n: The お makes 金 sound more polite; お金 is the usual everyday word.

2.6.n: Marks お金 as what you pay.

2.7.n: The ば conditional form of 払う sets payment as the condition for what follows.

3.0.n: Combines with でも to allow any choice of food.

3.1.n: After 何, it forms 何でも, expressing unrestricted choice rather than a contrast.

3.3.n: Asks about quantity on its own; with でも, it allows any number of items.

3.4.n: After いくつ, it shows there is no limit on the number you can eat.

4.0.n: The ability form of 食べる; although the same form can express being eaten, ability is intended here.

4.1.n: Turns the preceding description into a noun-like unit so it can define 食べ放題.

4.2.n: Politely completes the definition begun with 食べ放題は in line 2.

0.lit: However, the meaning is completely different, I tell you!
0.tip: 全然 can strengthen 違う even without a negative ending.

1.lit: In Japan, as for バイキング, it is the idea of all-you-can-eat.
1.tip: ということです explains what the quoted term means here.

2.lit: As for all-you-can-eat, if you pay money once,
2.tip: 払えば uses ば to introduce a condition, and the sentence continues into the next lines.

3.tip: A question word followed by でも allows any choice or quantity.

4.lit: It is being able to eat.
4.tip: こと turns the whole description from the previous lines into the definition of 食べ放題.
